name: Fathom Analytics
category: Privacy-first web analytics / GDPR-compliant Google Analytics alternative
teamSize: 2-3 (Jack Ellis sole owner since Dec 2024; Paul Jarvis retired to part-time freelance designer)
founder: Jack Ellis (developer) & Paul Jarvis (designer, author of Company of One); original technical collaborator Danny van Kooten departed Dec 2018
launchedYear: 2018 (Paul Jarvis tweet mockup Apr 2018; paid Fathom Pro after open-source version; V2 relaunch Nov 2019 with Jack Ellis)
problem: Google Analytics is a surveillance machine: bloated 45KB+ script, cookie banners, personal data harvested for ads; website owners only need simple traffic numbers without compromising visitors
customer: Website owners, bloggers, SaaS companies, Fortune 100 clients (GitHub, IBM, Hulu per founder statements), government organizations
valueProposition: Simple, privacy-first website analytics: sub-2KB script, no cookies, no personal data stored, no consent banner required — software company not advertising company, from $14/mo historically
mvp: Tweet mockup (Apr 2018) → open-source Go version with Danny van Kooten (millions of downloads, 6,000+ GitHub stars) → paid hosted Fathom Pro; Jack Ellis rebuilt V2 from scratch on Laravel + Heroku + Redis queue (Nov 2019), tripling MRR
revenueEvidence: FACT: $100K+ ARR reached ~Nov 2020 (~2 years, founder milestones). FACT: thousands of paying customers; 450,000+ sites tracked (2023, founder). FACT: never outspends revenue; profitable; self-financed co-founder buyout Dec 2024. HYPOTHESIS (third-party, unverified): $5-10M ARR (Founder Ventures). HYPOTHESIS (third-party): $1M+/mo claimed by Beancount.io blog (2026) — unverified. Company has never published exact revenue.
pricing: FACT (historical): from $14/mo (100K pageviews) scaling to $44/mo (500K). FACT (2026, OperatorBook): entry plan $45/mo for up to 500K pageviews. 7-day free trial; no permanent free tier; every account is paying.
freeTierAndTrial: 7-day free trial, no long free tier. Open-source self-hostable version existed early (6,000+ stars, 1M+ Docker pulls) but commercial product is paid-only.
distribution: Paul Jarvis tweet mockup going mini-viral; open-source version popularity → paid conversion; Product Hunt (#4); word-of-mouth and developer trust; SEO ('Google Analytics alternative'); 25%-for-life affiliate program with super-low churn; demand-gated iteration (each step only taken on proven demand)
launchStrategy: Tweet mockup validation → open-source version → paid Pro version → near-death (co-founder exit Dec 2018, considered shutdown) → Jack Ellis rebuild V2 → MRR tripled → profitable salaries → Paul Jarvis retirement buyout Dec 2024 (Jack Ellis sole owner, deal negotiated in 24h, no outside money)
technology: V2: Laravel (PHP), Heroku PaaS auto-scaling, Redis-driven queue, split API/Collector/Billing architecture. Original V1 was Go. Custom analytics engine processing billions of pageviews.
aiUsage: Minimal — not core to product; focus is simplicity and privacy
complexity: LOW for MVP (pageview counter + dashboard); MEDIUM for scaled product (multi-region collection, background processing, EU compliance)
differentiation: Company-of-One philosophy as brand; radical privacy (minimum collection as identity); refusal to publish revenue as on-brand stance; 25% lifetime affiliates; profitable-without-funding proof
competitors: Google Analytics (free incumbent), Plausible, Simple Analytics, Umami, Pirsch, Matomo, privacy-analytics crowd
weaknesses: Zero revenue transparency (all current figures are guesses); premium pricing vs free GA; co-founder dependency resolved only via 2024 buyout; crowded category with cheaper rivals
zeroDollarFeasibility: YES — demand-gated bootstrapping: each stage funded by prior stage revenue; Heroku PaaS scaled with income; no ad spend; affiliate program pays from revenue
hundredMrrRelevance: EXTREME — the Company-of-One archetype: 2 people, zero funding, thousands of paying customers, self-financed succession; proves privacy analytics sustains premium pricing against a free giant
sources: Fathom blog 'From almost shutting down to tripling our MRR' — https://usefathom.com/blog/v2 (2019); Fathom founder interview — https://usefathom.com/blog/interview (2022); Fathom about page — https://usefathom.com/about; Fathom Framework podcast lessons — https://usefathom.com/blog/saas-lessons (2020); OperatorBook revenue profile — https://www.operatorbook.dev/stories/fathom-analytics-revenue-the-number-they-refuse-to-publish (2026); Founder Ventures case study — https://founderventures.io/cases/fathom (2026); StartupFounderStories $100K ARR — https://startupfounderstories.com/stories/fathom-analytics-jack-ellis
contradictionNote: Founder Ventures estimates $5-10M ARR (unverified third-party) vs Beancount.io blog claims '$1M+ monthly revenue' (2026, unverified, implausible vs customer math) vs company itself: zero published figures, only 'thousands of customers' and '450,000+ sites tracked'. Treat all current revenue as order-of-magnitude guesses; the only anchored figure is $100K+ ARR (Nov 2020).

name: Simple Analytics
category: Privacy-first web analytics / GDPR-compliant Google Analytics alternative
teamSize: 2 (Adriaan van Rossum, developer; Iron Brands joined 2022 for marketing/ops). No investors, 100% founder-owned
founder: Adriaan van Rossum (self-taught developer, Amsterdam; ex-freelance); co-operator Iron Brands joined 2022
launchedYear: 2018 (2 months idea-to-MVP; Product Hunt Sep 2018 #3 of day + Privacy Golden Kitten #3; Hacker News front page #1 for 9 hours)
problem: Installing the GA snippet hands all visitor data to Google for ads; GA is complex, bloated, clunky with annoying cookie banners; freelancers forced to install it for clients felt it was wrong
customer: Privacy-conscious website owners, bloggers, SMBs buying into the privacy mission; businesses reached via direct outreach in later years
valueProposition: Track visitors without cookies and without a cookie banner — just pageviews, referrers, screen sizes in a clean dashboard; embeddable public dashboards; privacy as the cause, not just a feature
mvp: Graph of pageviews + lists of top pages, referrals, screen sizes only — no visitor tracking at all initially; built in ~2 months; launched on HN from a bench in Amsterdam; first 30 paying customers from launch day (~30K pageview spike)
revenueEvidence: FACT (founder blog): $30K ARR Oct 2019. FACT (founder, Indie Hackers 2020): $6K MRR May 2020. FACT (founder interview 2020): ~$6.7K MRR / ~$80K ARR, 471 paying customers Jul 2020. FACT (founder): stuck at ~$11K MRR until Iron joined 2022; passed $30K MRR after. FACT (2024 year review): 35.5-36K MRR, 1,330 paying customers, +36% YoY, $0 funding. INFERENCE (third-party): ~$39.6K MRR / 1,317 subs (Systemaic 2026); ~$500K/yr (RightBlogger 2026).
pricing: FACT (2026): self-serve from EUR 20/mo; free-forever tier exists. Historical: paid-from-start, briefly tried free (signups but no paid conversion), reverted to paid.
freeTierAndTrial: Free-forever tier seeds brand and word-of-mouth; embeddable public dashboards act as viral loop. No credit-card trial mechanics disclosed.
distribution: SEO is #1 channel ('Google Analytics alternative', privacy-analytics searches); serial Hacker News relaunches at each milestone ($30K ARR 261pts, $4K MRR 288pts, $100K ARR); Product Hunt 370 upvotes; open-metrics page as content engine; affiliate program; embeddable graphs; newsletters; rejected Google/Facebook ads on principle; later direct business outreach + onboarding pop-up with personal replies
launchStrategy: Quit job to force motivation (kept 1-week/mo freelancing to fund gap) → 2-month MVP → WIP-community feedback → PH + HN launch → open /metrics page as marketing → 3 years product-only stall at $11K MRR → marketing co-founder joins 2022 → $30K+ MRR → transparency dialed back once it had done its job
technology: UNKNOWN stack details (founder self-taught developer; bare-metal early platform tracking pageviews only). Privacy-safe by architecture: no cookies, no fingerprinting.
aiUsage: Minimal — AI search (OpenAI/Bing answers) emerging as discovery source; not part of product
complexity: LOW for MVP (pageview graph + 3 lists); LOW-MEDIUM full product (dashboard embeds, affiliates, open metrics)
differentiation: Radical revenue transparency as growth channel (monthly open page with MRR, costs, profit); mission-led buying ('customers buy the cause'); serial HN milestone relaunches; privacy-principled refusal of surveillance ads
competitors: Google Analytics (free), Fathom, Plausible, Umami, Pirsch, Cabin, Beam (defunct 2026)
weaknesses: 7-year grind to ~$40K MRR (slow by VC standards); stopped live revenue dashboard (transparency retreated); only ~5 pages drive real organic traffic (lumpy earned-media dependence); ~3.4% monthly churn reported Jul 2024
zeroDollarFeasibility: YES — freelancing 1 week/mo funded the gap; bare-metal hosting; zero ad spend (principled); content + transparency as free distribution
hundredMrrRelevance: HIGH — textbook slow-compound indie: $900 MRR at 6 months → $23K at 60 months → ~$40K MRR at year 7; proves distribution (not product) was the bottleneck and a marketing co-founder unlocked it
sources: Simple Analytics $30K ARR blog — https://www.simpleanalytics.com/blog/how-we-hit-our-30k-annual-recurring-revenue-milestone (2019); Simple Analytics milestones press page — https://www.simpleanalytics.com/press/milestones (2025); Milestones case study '$36K/mo' — https://milestones.so/case-study/simple-analytics; Systemaic teardown — https://www.systemaic.com/teardowns/simple-analytics (2026); OperatorBook revenue profile — https://www.operatorbook.dev/stories/simple-analytics-revenue-500k-bootstrapped-ga-rival (2026); Starter Story '$35K MRR' — https://www.starterstory.com/simple-analytics-breakdown (2024); SaaSStarterStack co-founder interview — https://saasstarterstack.com/interviews/simple-analytics; Daniliants Ventures founder interview — https://daniliants.ventures/fi/podcastit/founder-story-why-adriaan-decided-to-create-his-own-google-analytics-alternative/ (2020)
contradictionNote: Starter Story (Nov 2024) says '$35K/mo' and '1300+ users, $32K MRR within months of launch' — the latter conflates later figures with launch era (launch yielded ~30 paying customers, not $32K MRR). Systemaic reports verified $39,577.53 MRR across 1,317 subs (2026) vs RightBlogger ~$500K/yr estimate — directionally consistent (~$475K ARR), treat as approximate.

technology: UNKNOWN exact stack (not verified via primary source). Open-source core on GitHub with self-hosting option; server-side (backend) tracking integration offered.

name: Cabin
category: Privacy-first + carbon-conscious web analytics / ethical GA alternative
status: Active (independent since Jan 2025 after Normally studio closure; NOT dead — verify confusion below)
teamSize: 1 (Nic Mulvaney, sole owner/operator via Nic Mulvaney LTD; previously incubated inside Normally studio team)
founder: Nic Mulvaney (creator and lead developer; NOT 'Nico Cernek' — no primary source supports that name; correction recorded). Incubated at Normally studio (clients: IKEA, Spotify, Logitech, BBC) from 2020.
launchedYear: 2020 (born/incubated at Normally studio; public product; independence announced Jan 2025)
problem: Analytics tools force a privacy-vs-insight tradeoff and ignore emissions; conscious companies (plus governments, universities, Fortune 500) want cookieless GDPR/CCPA compliance AND carbon accountability in one script
customer: Solo developers, conscious companies, governments, universities, Fortune 500 orgs, agencies/studios managing client sites
valueProposition: Privacy-first AND carbon-conscious analytics: no cookies, no IP storage, no fingerprinting (novel Last-Modified-cache unique-visitor method), 100% renewable-energy hosting, carbon footprint reporting, EU data storage
mvp: Studio side-project: privacy-by-design analytics with non-relational aggregate-only data model; unique-visitor counting via HTTP Last-Modified cache trick (no identifiers of any kind); carbon reporting as differentiator from the start
revenueEvidence: UNKNOWN — no public revenue figures found. FACT: survived 5 years as studio passion project without growth pressure; now sole-operator commercial product with three paid tiers + free tier. Traffic/revenue undisclosed.
pricing: FACT (pricing page, fetched 2026): Free $0 (1 domain, 10K pageviews/mo, 30-day retention); Plus $14/mo (10 domains, 100K pageviews, 12-mo retention, custom events, carbon reporting, API); Scale $45/mo (unlimited domains, 5M pageviews, unlimited retention, GSC integration, branded client dashboards). Yearly = 2 months free.
freeTierAndTrial: Free tier: 1 site, 10K pageviews/mo, no credit card. Full MCP access on every plan including free. Data export included.
distribution: Studio-client halo (IKEA/Spotify/BBC credibility); technical content marketing (deep GDPR/cookieless explainers, Last-Modified method write-ups); comparison pages (vs GA, vs Plausible, vs Matomo); 'How Green Is Your Website' tool; GitHub presence; agency/studio channel (client-ready branded dashboards)
launchStrategy: Incubated inside client-funded studio (no revenue pressure for ~5 years) → studio closure Jan 2025 → founder buyout-by-default (wholly owned, operational reality formalized) → indie commercialization with agency-flavored Scale tier
technology: AWS EU (Ireland) storage; edge collection endpoints (Ireland, Frankfurt, Mumbai, Singapore, memory-only forwarding); IP held in memory for country lookup then discarded; browser-cache Last-Modified counting; status page + GitHub org present.
aiUsage: LATER ADDITION — dedicated /ai page, 'Monitor AI agent traffic' on Scale, MCP access on all plans; not part of MVP
complexity: MEDIUM (novel identifier-free counting R&D; multi-region collection; carbon modeling; compliance documentation across 10+ privacy regimes)
differentiation: Only product in slice combining privacy + carbon reporting; most technically rigorous cookieless method (Last-Modified cache, published write-up); legally candid docs (admits in-memory IP processing is processing); MCP/AI-agent traffic monitoring early
competitors: Google Analytics, Plausible, Fathom, Simple Analytics, Umami, Pirsch, Matomo, other carbon trackers (Website Carbon Calculator)
weaknesses: Zero revenue transparency; single-operator bus factor post-studio; crowded category with better-funded rivals; carbon angle unproven as purchase driver; 'Nico Cernek' misattribution floating in secondary sources
zeroDollarFeasibility: YES — 5 years studio-subsidized (client work paid the bills); AWS costs only; passion-project economics before commercialization
hundredMrrRelevance: MEDIUM-HIGH — studio-incubation is a replicable zero-cost path (fund R&D with client work); agency Scale tier ($45/mo, branded client dashboards) is the monetization pattern to copy

complexity: LOW-MEDIUM (bought infra; focused on dashboard + funnels; two part-timers shipped in 3 months)
differentiation: Lowest-price guarantee framing + linear predictable pricing; only budget player with funnels/cohorts; shared-account-friendly (anti-Netflix-seat-pricing stance); infra-transparency (public telemetry.sh build log)

technology: ReactJS frontend + CapacitorJS (mobile) + Electron (desktop); NodeJS/TypeScript + Go backend; DigitalOcean hosting; MongoDB + ClickHouse data layer.
aiUsage: UNKNOWN — no AI positioning found in reviewed sources
complexity: MEDIUM (cross-platform clients + real-time pipeline + data-volume scaling as solo dev; ClickHouse for scale)

sources: Starter Story breakdown — https://www.starterstory.com/logsnag-breakdown (2024); GrowthLessons waitlist story — https://growthlessons.co/shayan-built-a-950-person-waitlist-for-his-app-with-no-audience-heres-how/ (2022); Bootstrappers pricing story — https://bootstrappers.com/if-customers-dont-pay-for-a-common-service-make-a-better-one-and-profit/ (2022); IH feedback-tool post — https://www.indiehackers.com/post/i-accidentally-built-a-powerful-feedback-collection-tool-e704e3013a (2022); BetaList — https://betalist.com/startups/logsnag (2022); LogSnag docs quick-start + /log API — https://docs.logsnag.com/quick-start; MakerStack review (secondary pricing) — https://makerstack.co/reviews/logsnag-review/ (2026); EmitKit comparison (secondary pricing) — https://www.emitkit.com/comparisons/logsnag (2025)

name: Splitbee
category: All-in-one analytics + conversion (page analytics, funnels, A/B testing, email automation) — DEAD-END failure case
status: Dead (acqui-hired by Vercel Oct 25, 2022; standalone product sunset; site now a thank-you page)
teamSize: 2 (brothers Tobias Lins, founder/CEO + Timo Lins, design; joined Vercel as staff/product roles)
founder: Tobias Lins (founder/CEO, ex-paramedic turned full-stack dev) & Timo Lins (co-founder, design/UI; timo.sh)
problem: Analytics tools were neither snappy nor fun; brands needed visits + funnels + experiments + email automation in one friendly tool instead of stitching GA + Optimizely + Mailchimp
customer: Brands, developers, Vercel/Next.js users (post-acquisition: every Vercel customer got audience analytics)
valueProposition: 'Your friendly all-in-one analytics tool': track visits, build funnels, run A/B tests, create email automations — real-time, privacy-friendly, snappy and fun to use
mvp: Tobias's first releases (analytics + conversion basics) → Timo joined for full facelift (bee logo, landing page, mobile-friendly dashboard) → all-in-one expansion (experiments, automations)
revenueEvidence: UNKNOWN — no founder-published revenue found. SECONDARY (LinkedIn directory): '$1M-$10M range' — unverified directory noise. The exit was a talent/product acqui-hire (terms undisclosed), not a revenue event.
pricing: UNKNOWN exact tiers (product sunset; pricing page gone). Era-typical freemium SaaS assumed — never fabricate.
freeTierAndTrial: UNKNOWN (sunset product; historical free-tier details unverified).
distribution: Design-led virality (cute bee brand, polished dashboard screenshots); indie-hacker/Twitter audience; Next.js ecosystem fit (the strategic reason Vercel bought it); post-acquisition distribution became Vercel's own changelog (audience metrics beta Oct 2022)
launchStrategy: Brother-built indie tool (2020) → design facelift as growth lever → ecosystem-fit exit: Vercel needed first-party privacy-friendly analytics for its frontend cloud → Oct 2022 acquisition → founders joined Vercel (Tobias: Tech Lead on Observability/Web Analytics/Speed Insights/Logs; Timo: Design lead) → standalone sunset
technology: JavaScript stack (React/Redux frontend per founder profiles; Node.js, GraphQL, AWS Lambda backend; Puppeteer usage). Post-acquisition rebuilt inside Vercel's analytics infrastructure.
aiUsage: UNKNOWN — no AI positioning in its era (pre-LLM analytics)
complexity: MEDIUM (real-time analytics + A/B testing + email automation in one product — broad scope for 2 people)
differentiation: All-in-one breadth (analytics + experiments + email) with indie friendliness; design quality as moat (Timo's facelift); real-time + privacy-friendly before it was table stakes
competitors: Google Analytics/Optimize, Plausible, Fathom, Mixpanel/Amplitude (era), Vercel's own eventual analytics (its acquirer)
weaknesses: FATAL AS STANDALONE: scope too broad for 2 people; no public revenue traction; exit = surrender of independence (the anti-indie outcome); users forced to migrate to Vercel platform; brand dissolved to a thank-you page
zeroDollarFeasibility: YES for build (two brothers, no funding) — but the lesson is strategic: zero-cost building still ends in acqui-hire when scope outruns distribution
hundredMrrRelevance: HIGH as failure-case archetype — the honest dead-end: a beloved indie analytics tool that 'succeeded' only by ceasing to exist. Teaches ecosystem-fit exits (build what a platform needs) vs sustainable independence (Fathom/Simple Analytics path)
sources: Vercel acquisition announcement — https://vercel.com/blog/vercel-acquires-splitbee (2022); BusinessWire acquisition — https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20221025005915/en/Vercel-Acquires-Splitbee-to-Expand-Its-First-Party-Privacy-Friendly-Analytics-Offering (2022); Splitbee sunset page — https://splitbee.io/ ('sunset... mission continues at Vercel. – Tobi & Timo'); Timo Lins portfolio — https://timo.sh/splitbee (2020); Tobias Lins site (Vercel Tech Lead, Splitbee founder) — https://tobi.sh/; Vercel changelog audience metrics — https://vercel.com/changelog/enhanced-audience-metrics-now-available-in-vercel-analytics (2022)
contradictionNote: No revenue contradictions (nothing published). name: GoatCounter
category: Open-source web analytics / donation-funded hosted service + self-hosted binary
teamSize: 1 (Martin Tournoij, arp242; full-time on GoatCounter funded by GitHub Sponsors with little other income)
founder: Martin Tournoij (Dutch developer; accessibility + open-source advocate; GitHub @arp242)
launchedYear: UNKNOWN (exact launch date unverified; public development and hosted service established by 2020; founder 'why' essay documents origin)
problem: Existing analytics are either complex marketing suites needing training or too simplistic; all hosted options priced for business (≥$10/mo) — nothing affordable for personal/hobby sites; GA's pervasive tracking de-google-fies nothing
customer: Indie developers, bloggers, open-source projects, hobby sites, photographers/personal sites, small-to-medium businesses (non-commercial free; commercial paid/self-hosted)
valueProposition: Easy, meaningful, privacy-friendly analytics as open-source: no cookies, no personal data, accessibility-first, single-binary self-hosting — free hosted service for reasonable (non-commercial) use, funded by donations
mvp: Solo-built Go binary: pageviews, referrers, campaigns, browsers, countries, screen sizes, events, filtering — SQLite default (PostgreSQL for scale); same codebase for hosted + self-hosted (no crippled community edition)
revenueEvidence: UNKNOWN — no revenue figures published. FACT: donation-funded via GitHub Sponsors tiers ($5/$15/$30/$100/mo + custom); founder states full-time work with 'little other source of income'. No subscriptions on hosted service per primary sources (MakerStack claims $15/mo Business tier — secondary, conflicts with 'no paid tier' reports; verify before citing).
pricing: FACT (primary): hosted free for reasonable use ('millions of pageviews/day isn't'); donations via GitHub Sponsors; self-hosted completely free without restrictions. SECONDARY (MakerStack 2026): Free non-commercial unlimited + Business $15/mo — conflicts with unsubbed.co 'There is no paid tier'; treat paid-tier existence as UNVERIFIED.
freeTierAndTrial: Free hosted for non-commercial/personal use with no pageview limits stated; no trial mechanics (it's just free); self-hosting free for everyone including commercial.
distribution: GitHub open-source discovery (stars/forks as trust); Hacker News; indie-dev word-of-mouth; accessibility-first positioning (differentiator in category); 'de-Google-fy the internet' mission framing; zero paid marketing
launchStrategy: Scratch-own-itch (frozen original idea, wrote GoatCounter instead) → open-source from day one → donation-supported full-time maintenance → honesty-as-pricing ('I need to pay the bills' essay) → self-hosting as the commercial escape valve
technology: Go single binary; SQLite default, PostgreSQL for scale; no JS dependencies; no database server needed for small sites; $5-6/mo VPS self-hosting viable.
complexity: LOW-MEDIUM (single binary, SQLite; distinct-URL cardinality is the scaling bottleneck per README, not raw pageviews)
differentiation: Most honest funding model in slice (donations, no paywall theater); only same-codebase hosted+self-hosted (no enterprise-gated features); accessibility-first build; deliberately vague free-use line ('reasonable') keeps barrier near zero
competitors: Google Analytics (free), Matomo (self-host complexity), Plausible ($9+/mo), Fathom, Cabin, Tinylytics
weaknesses: Fragile funding (donations, no SLA — unsuitable for mission-critical commercial use per third-party); no formal paid tier = no growth engine; design 'will not win beauty contests'; founder single-income dependency on goodwill
zeroDollarFeasibility: EXTREME — the purest zero-cost product in the slice: free for users, ~$5/mo VPS to self-host, open-source; sustainability question is the founder's income, not the tech
hundredMrrRelevance: MEDIUM as business, EXTREME as philosophy — proves the floor: a one-person open-source analytics tool can serve the whole non-commercial web on donations; the anti-monetization pole against Fathom's premium pole

name: Tinylytics
category: Joyful privacy analytics + site-health monitoring for small sites (pageviews, uptime/SSL, events, kudos, content checks)
teamSize: 1 (Vincent Ritter; founder answers every support email personally)
founder: Vincent Ritter (indie dev; previously Micro.blog-adjacent work; blog-first builder)
launchedYear: 2023 (launched June 2023; MVP built over a weekend, live the following Monday; subscriptions added 2 weeks later)
problem: Analytics SaaS is boring and stressful — number-fixation anxiety; Plausible-class pricing ($190/yr) too steep for small blogs; nobody bundles pageviews + uptime + broken-link/content checks + fun (hit counters, kudos buttons) for indie sites
customer: Small websites, personal blogs, side projects, indie developers (explicitly NOT enterprise — 'fair usage above 1M hits/mo, reach out')
valueProposition: A joyful, JOMO analytics tool: privacy-first cookie-free stats + automatic uptime/SSL/domain monitoring + event tracking + content monitoring (broken links, spellcheck) + 90s hit counter and kudos — unlimited hits on every paid plan
mvp: Weekend build: pageview stats with 10x Plausible's headroom at half the cost; teased without detail → 20 accounts day one → 100 accounts in 2 weeks → optional subscriptions added → 10 paid subs in 48h → €160 MRR / ~€400 revenue at day 17 (yearly plans outsold expectations)

pricing: FACT (billing docs + changelog, 2026): Zen $7/mo ($70/yr, 2 sites); Pro $14/mo ($140/yr, 20 sites); Ultra $29/mo ($290/yr, 50 sites). ALL plans: identical analytics, unlimited hits forever (fair-use chat above ~1M hits/mo), unlimited retention, API, webhooks, uptime/SSL monitoring. Prices locked forever for existing customers.
freeTierAndTrial: 14-day free trial (all features, no card). NO free plan — deliberately dropped: 'We cannot compete on free. We are bootstrapped and here for the long run.' Legacy free accounts grandfathered.
distribution: Founder blog + launch post (first sub came from blog post); indie-dev word-of-mouth (Plausible-switcher testimonials); public changelog (updates.tinylytics.app) as marketing; live demo of own stats; planned podcast ads (RelayFM/indie shows); SEO comparison posts ('alternative to X')
launchStrategy: Weekend MVP → tease → 20 day-one accounts → 100 in 2 weeks → paid option only when legs confirmed → slow-steady positioning ('buy groceries, pay servers, happy days') → 2025-26: killed hit caps entirely as differentiator vs metered rivals
technology: UNKNOWN stack details. Ships: real-time webhooks, full API, rotating-salt unique-hit counting (privacy-preserving), Europe-hosted, AI-context spike alerts (Ultra).
aiUsage: LATER ADDITION — spike alerts 'with AI context' on Ultra; not core, not in MVP
complexity: LOW for MVP (pageview stats weekend build); MEDIUM full product (uptime fleet, content monitoring, webhooks, team access)
differentiation: JOMO positioning vs anxiety-inducing dashboards; unlimited-hits-forever vs every metered rival; site-count (not usage) pricing; fun differentiators (hit counter, kudos); founder-personal support as feature; anti-free sustainability stance
competitors: Plausible (the switch-from source), Fathom, Simple Analytics, Cabin, GoatCounter, Umami, uptime tools (Oh Dear, UptimeRobot)
weaknesses: Tiny scale (hundreds of customers implied); no public current revenue; single-founder support burden; unlimited-hits promise untested at scale; JOMO niche caps willingness-to-pay

hundredMrrRelevance: HIGH — fastest validation in slice (paid subs 2 weeks post-MVP, 10 in 48h); proves site-count pricing + unlimited usage is a viable anti-metering wedge; 'drop free, keep trial' is the counter-lesson to LogSnag/GoatCounter free funnels

name: Oh Dear
category: Website monitoring / uptime + whole-site health (SSL, broken links, DNS, Lighthouse, cron, certs, mixed content)
teamSize: 2 (co-founders only, zero employees; split: Mattias support/admin/monitoring-dev, Freek core PHP/crawler)
founder: Mattias Geniar (sysadmin, ex-managed-hosting; cron.weekly newsletter ~11K subs) & Freek Van der Herten (agency owner Spatie; prolific Laravel open-source; newsletter ~7K subs)
launchedYear: 2018 (private beta 2017; public launch Jan 11, 2018 — prices decided same evening; first paying customer in 30 minutes; 32 paid by month-end)
problem: Uptime tools ping only the homepage and assume the rest works — false confidence; SSL expiries, broken links, DNS changes, mixed content, cron failures discovered via customer complaints, not monitoring
customer: Agencies, Laravel/PHP developers, SMBs managing client sites; CraftCMS/Statamic/Laravel Nova integration users
valueProposition: Don't just monitor your homepage — monitor your entire site: uptime from multiple locations + cert/domain expiry + search-engine-style crawler (broken links, mixed content) + Lighthouse SEO/accessibility + cron/DNS/health — one flat price, all features
mvp: Uptime monitoring + certificate-expiry alerts + crawler (the day-one differentiator); built evenings/weekends on Laravel Spark (billing/VAT handled); dogfooded on Spatie + Nucleus sites; laravel-uptime-monitor open-source package (Nov 2016) as prototype
revenueEvidence: FACT (founders): ~$1.5K MRR at launch month end, Jan 2018 (32 customers; profitable month one, covered hosting). FACT (founder, 2020 blog): revenue numbers shared publicly for months. FACT (founder IH post Sep 2025): >$83K/mo, $1M ARR, 8 years in, 2 founders, no employees, no VC. SECONDARY (GetLatka): $126.5K revenue 2024 ($100K 2023) — flatly contradicts founder $1M ARR; treat aggregator as wrong or stale. 14B+ checks performed; 5.7M+ notifications sent (founder, 2022).
pricing: FACT: pay by number of sites monitored, all features included, no feature gating, no tiers. Free trial (10 days); NO permanent free tier ('free users cost money and rarely convert'). Exact per-site dollars UNKNOWN from verified sources.
freeTierAndTrial: 10-day free trial only. Explicit anti-free-tier stance is a documented positioning choice, opposite of LogSnag/GoatCounter funnels.
distribution: Pre-built audiences (both founders' Twitter + newsletters ~18K combined + blogs/RSS); 500-person pre-launch email list → 10% converted (~20 paying, ~$1.5K MRR day one); Laravel News pickup; Product Hunt Product of the Day; API-first (75% of GUI) enabling integrations; framework integrations (CraftCMS/Statamic/Laravel Nova) as channels; paid ads and outsourced content failed (near-zero ROI, founder-regretted)
launchStrategy: Years of audience-building BEFORE product (open-source packages, newsletter, tweets, screenshots/mockups) → private beta → priced-at-launch-evening → Laravel-community launch → 8 years of build-in-public compounding → $1M ARR with zero employees
technology: Deliberately boring: Laravel/PHP, MySQL, Redis, ClickHouse for analytics; bare-metal dispatch + ~50 VMs across DigitalOcean/Vultr/AWS for global coverage; 1M+ monitoring jobs/day.
aiUsage: UNKNOWN — no AI positioning found in reviewed sources
complexity: MEDIUM (global monitoring fleet, crawler at search-engine scale, 14B checks; boring stack keeps it operable by 2 people)
differentiation: Whole-site (not homepage) monitoring; crawler as day-one wedge; flat all-features pricing; no-free-tier conviction; audience-first launch (list → 10% conversion); dual-founder complementary split (sysadmin + dev)
competitors: UptimeRobot, Pingdom, StatusCake, Better Stack (Better Uptime), Datadog Synthetics (upmarket), cron-specific tools
weaknesses: Refusal to hire caps velocity (founders acknowledge); paid acquisition proven worthless for them (channel risk if audiences decay); aggregator data massively understates them (visibility gap); monitoring-commodity price pressure
zeroDollarFeasibility: YES — hobby economics (time = 'free', first income covered hosting); Laravel Spark + existing servers; audiences built free over years; profitable from month one
hundredMrrRelevance: EXTREME — the $1M ARR / 2-founder / 0-employee proof; audience-before-product is the replicable zero-cost engine (500-list → $1.5K MRR day one); 'boring stack + no free tier + no employees' is a complete operating system for the lab
sources: IH $1M ARR build-in-public post — https://www.indiehackers.com/post/tech/growing-a-web-monitoring-tool-to-1m-arr-by-building-in-public-X876kKI7Olsf4YBI8FWb (2025); SaaSrat founder interview ($1M+ ARR, no free tier, stack) — https://saasrat.com/blog/oh-dear-founder-interviews/ (2026); Freek 2.0 launch recap (first customer in 30 min, 32 paid) — https://freek.dev/2343-oh-dear-20-has-been-launched (2022); Mattias distribution post — https://ma.ttias.be/how-are-users-finding-our-saas/ (2020); Mattias IH launch post — https://www.indiehackers.com/post/the-market-lacked-the-tool-we-wanted-so-we-built-it-ourselves-hMXCg9e0X1P6mITm5Xxf (2018); Oh Dear about — https://ohdear.app/about; GetLatka profile (secondary, disputed) — https://getlatka.com/companies/oh-dear
contradictionNote: DIRECT CLASH: founders claim $1M ARR / >$83K/mo (Sep 2025 IH post, repeated in 2026 SaaSrat interview) vs GetLatka '$126.5K revenue 2024, $100K 2023'. Verbatim: IH 'bringing in $1M ARR' vs GetLatka 'generates an estimated $126.5K in annual revenue'.
